response.query: How many specimens and orientations per material are needed (power analysis) to detect a 10% difference in H or E between source units or functional groups?
response.answer: To detect a 10% difference in H or E, typically 10-20 specimens per orientation per material are needed for adequate power analysis. Exact numbers depend on variability and desired confidence level. Generally, more samples improve accuracy.

results.title: Magnetic saturation
results.content: **Magnetic saturation** - a phenomenon of non-linearity of magnetic properties of magnetic materials at high amplitude of magnetic excitation.1)2)3)4) At complete magnetic saturation, the values of magnetisation *M* (A/m) or magnetic polarisation *J* (T) reach the highest possible values of **saturation magnetisation** *Msat* or **saturation polarisation** *Jsat*, respectively, which are also a function of the chemical composition of the material and temperature.5). However, at higher excitation the onset of saturation decreases the value of permeability, eventually (at sufficiently high amplitude) making the effective permeability similar to that of non-magnetic materials (i.e. The inductance (and hence impedance) of the associated windings decreases significantly, leading to inrush and fault currents,7) which can be dangerous to the reliability or operation of the electromagnetic device. Illustration of magnetic field strength *H*, flux density *B*, magnetisation *M*, and polarisation *J* in a **ferromagnet**; all three vector quantities *H*, *M* and *B* can be at different angles due to energy of anisotropy; in the shown state the material is close to saturation, but not yet fully saturated because the direction of *M*, *J*, and *B* vectors is not yet parallel to the applied *H*.
